name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_STATEMENT3_Q01 - Cellular tissue and organ levels of organisation

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the levels of body organisation in animals:

Statement I: In sponges, cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates exhibiting a cellular level of organisation.

Statement II: In coelenterates, cells performing the same function are arranged into tissues, exhibiting a tissue level of organisation.

Statement III: Members of Platyhelminthes exhibit organ system level of organisation with a complete digestive tract.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Animals are classified into progressive grades of organisation including cellular, tissue, organ, and organ system levels.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Proposition
Sponges are multicellular organisms where individual cells display division of labour as loose aggregates without true tissue formation, representing the cellular level. Thus, the first proposition is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Proposition
In coelenterates, similar cells are coordinated into functional tissues to perform specialized tasks, representing the tissue level. Thus, the second proposition is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
Platyhelminthes exhibit organ level of organisation, and their digestive tract has only a single opening, making it incomplete rather than a complete organ system. Thus, the third proposition is incorrect.

Step 5: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
Only the first and second propositions are scientifically correct. Therefore, the correct combination is that statements I and II only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_STATEMENT3_Q02 - Radial and bilateral symmetry patterns across phyla

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding body symmetry in animals:

Statement I: When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry.

Statement II: Adult echinoderms exhibit bilateral symmetry, whereas their larvae exhibit radial symmetry.

Statement III: Annelids and arthropods exhibit bilateral symmetry where the body can be divided into identical right and left halves in only one plane.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Symmetry reflects the morphological body plan and the number of planes capable of dividing an animal into identical mirror images.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Proposition
Radial symmetry is defined by any longitudinal plane passing through the central axis partitioning the organism into two identical halves, as seen in coelenterates and ctenophores. Thus, the first proposition is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Proposition
Echinoderms display bilateral symmetry during their free-swimming larval phase and transform into pentaradial symmetry during adulthood. The proposition inverts these life stages. Thus, the second proposition is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
Bilateral symmetry enables division into equivalent left and right antimers along a single sagittal plane, characteristic of annelids and arthropods. Thus, the third proposition is factually accurate.

Step 5: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
The first and third propositions represent correct biological principles, while the second proposition contains an inverted developmental claim. Therefore, the correct combination is that statements I and III only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_STATEMENT3_Q03 - Coelomic cavities and their embryonic mesodermal linings

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the body cavity (coelom) in animals:

Statement I: Platyhelminthes are pseudocoelomate animals because their body cavity is lined by scattered mesodermal pouches.

Statement II: In Aschelminthes, the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm; instead, mesoderm is present as scattered pouches between ectoderm and endoderm.

Statement III: Annelids, arthropods, molluscs, and chordates possess a true coelom lined completely by mesoderm.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The presence, nature, and mesodermal lining of the cavity between the body wall and gut wall serve as essential criteria in animal classification.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Proposition
Platyhelminthes are acoelomate animals completely devoid of a body cavity, with solid parenchyma filling the space between gut and body wall. Thus, the first proposition is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Proposition
Aschelminthes possess a pseudocoelom characterized by scattered pouches of mesodermal cells situated between the ectoderm and endoderm rather than a continuous peritoneal epithelium. Thus, the second proposition is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
Animals from Annelida through Chordata possess a secondary body cavity, or true coelom, lined entirely by mesoderm on both visceral and parietal surfaces. Thus, the third proposition is factually accurate.

Step 5: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
Only the second and third propositions accurately categorize coelom configurations. Therefore, the correct combination is that statements II and III only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_STATEMENT3_Q04 - Diagnostic features and physiology of phylum Porifera

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding phylum Porifera:

Statement I: Water enters through minute pores called ostia into the central spongocoel and exits through the osculum.

Statement II: Choanocytes or collar cells line the spongocoel and the canals, functioning in water circulation and food gathering.

Statement III: Sponges are hermaphrodite animals exhibiting internal fertilisation and indirect development with a larval stage.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sponges (phylum Porifera) are primitive multicellular, mostly marine animals defined by a canal system, collar cells, and distinct reproductive cycles.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Proposition
The aquiferous water canal system directs sea water inward via minute dermal ostia into the internal spongocoel cavity and discharges it outward via the terminal osculum. Thus, the first proposition is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Proposition
Flagellated collar cells, known as choanocytes, line the interior walls of the spongocoel and radial canals, driving the unidirectional flow of water and capturing organic particles. Thus, the second proposition is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
Poriferans are monoecious (hermaphrodites) producing both ova and spermatozoa within the same individual; fertilisation occurs internally, giving rise to morphologically distinct ciliated larvae. Thus, the third proposition is factually accurate.

Step 5: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
All three propositions correctly state the anatomical, cytological, and developmental traits of sponges. Therefore, the correct combination is that statements I, II and III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_STATEMENT3_Q05 - Body forms cnidoblasts and metagenesis in cnidarians

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria):

Statement I: Cnidoblasts contain stinging capsules or nematocysts and are used for anchorage, defense, and prey capture.

Statement II: In cnidarians exhibiting metagenesis, polyps produce medusae asexually, and medusae form polyps sexually.

Statement III: Corals possess an exoskeleton composed of calcium carbonate, and their digestion is strictly intracellular.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cnidarians are diploblastic, radially symmetrical organisms defined by cnidocytes, polymorphic polyp and medusa body plans, and metagenesis.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Proposition
Cnidoblasts (cnidocytes) located on the tentacles and body wall bear explosive nematocyst capsules specialized for anchoring the organism, capturing prey, and deterring predators. Thus, the first proposition is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Proposition
In polymorphic genera like Obelia, alternation of generations (metagenesis) occurs whereby sessile polyps bud medusae asexually, and free-swimming medusae produce gametes sexually to form polyps. Thus, the second proposition is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
Although corals secrete a rigid calcareous exoskeleton, digestion in all cnidarians is initially extracellular in the gastro-vascular cavity followed by intracellular digestion inside gastrodermal cells. Thus, the third proposition is incorrect.

Step 5: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
The first and second propositions are factually verified, whereas the third proposition falsely restricts digestion to intracellular processes alone. Therefore, the correct combination is that statements I and II only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_STATEMENT3_Q06 - Ciliated comb plates bioluminescence and ctenophore reproduction

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding phylum Ctenophora:

Statement I: The body of ctenophores bears eight external rows of ciliated comb plates which help in locomotion.

Statement II: Reproduction in ctenophores takes place by both asexual fragmentation and sexual means.

Statement III: Bioluminescence is well-marked in ctenophores, and their fertilisation is external with indirect development.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ctenophores (comb jellies or sea walnuts) are exclusively marine, diploblastic animals with tissue-level organisation and prominent locomotor comb plates.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Proposition
Ctenophore bodies are characterized by eight meridional rows of fused ciliary comb plates functioning in coordinated aquatic propulsion. Thus, the first proposition is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Proposition
Ctenophores do not reproduce asexually; reproduction occurs exclusively by sexual means through gametic fusion. Thus, the second proposition is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
Living ctenophores prominently emit light through bioluminescence, release gametes into sea water for external fertilisation, and undergo indirect development. Thus, the third proposition is factually accurate.

Step 5: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
Propositions one and three correctly outline the physiology and reproduction of ctenophores, while proposition two introduces an unobserved asexual mode. Therefore, the correct combination is that statements I and III only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_STATEMENT3_Q07 - Morphological comparisons between flatworms and roundworms

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding flatworms and roundworms:

Statement I: Platyhelminthes possess a complete digestive tract with a muscular pharynx and separate mouth and anal openings.

Statement II: Specialised cells called flame cells help in osmoregulation and excretion in Platyhelminthes.

Statement III: In Aschelminthes, sexes are separate (dioecious), and females are often longer than males.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Flatworms (Platyhelminthes) and roundworms (Aschelminthes) display clear evolutionary divergences in body cavity, digestive completeness, and sexual dimorphism.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Proposition
Platyhelminthes have an incomplete digestive system with only a single opening acting as mouth and anus, whereas a complete tract with a muscular pharynx belongs to Aschelminthes. Thus, the first proposition is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Proposition
Flame cells (solenocytes) in flatworms represent specialized protonephridial units regulating ionic balance, water content, and nitrogenous waste excretion. Thus, the second proposition is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
Aschelminthes are dioecious with distinct morphological sexual dimorphism where adult females regularly exceed males in length. Thus, the third proposition is factually accurate.

Step 5: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
Propositions two and three represent accurate anatomical descriptions, while proposition one misattributes roundworm digestive features to flatworms. Therefore, the correct combination is that statements II and III only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_STATEMENT3_Q08 - Locomotion circulation and metameric segmentation in annelids

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding phylum Annelida:

Statement I: Annelids possess longitudinal and circular muscles in their body wall which help in locomotion.

Statement II: Aquatic annelids like Nereis possess lateral unjointed appendages called parapodia which aid in swimming.

Statement III: The neural system consists of paired ganglia connected by lateral nerves to a double ventral nerve cord.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Annelids are true coelomate, metamerically segmented worms possessing closed circulation, muscular body walls, and centralized ventral nerve cords.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Proposition
The body wall of annelids is lined by an antagonistic musculature of outer circular and inner longitudinal fibers which generate peristaltic waves for burrowing and crawl locomotion. Thus, the first proposition is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Proposition
Marine errant annelids such as Nereis possess fleshy, lateral muscular outgrowths called parapodia that provide hydrostatic paddles for swimming. Thus, the second proposition is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
The annelid nervous system comprises segmented paired ganglia joined to a circumpharyngeal ring and continuing posteriorly as a double solid ventral nerve cord. Thus, the third proposition is factually accurate.

Step 5: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
All three propositions correctly state established neurological and locomotory features of annelids. Therefore, the correct combination is that statements I, II and III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_STATEMENT3_Q09 - Exoskeleton respiratory systems and appendages of arthropods

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding phylum Arthropoda:

Statement I: The body of arthropods is covered by a chitinous exoskeleton and consists of head, thorax, and abdomen.

Statement II: Respiratory organs in arthropods include gills, book gills, book lungs, or a tracheal system.

Statement III: Arthropods possess a closed circulatory system and excrete nitrogenous wastes through nephridia.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Arthropods form the largest animal phylum characterized by a protective chitinous cuticle, jointed limbs, hemocoelic open circulation, and varied respiratory organs.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Proposition
Arthropods exhibit distinct tagmosis into head, thorax, and abdomen encased within an impermeable cuticle composed of chitin and proteins. Thus, the first proposition is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Proposition
Depending on aquatic or terrestrial ecology, arthropods utilize gills (crustaceans), book gills (horseshoe crabs), book lungs (scorpions/spiders), or tracheal air tubes (insects). Thus, the second proposition is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
Arthropods possess an open circulatory system where hemolymph bathes tissue sinuses directly, and excretion typically occurs via Malpighian tubules rather than annelid nephridia. Thus, the third proposition is incorrect.

Step 5: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
The first and second propositions are biologically accurate, whereas the third proposition incorrectly reports closed circulation and nephridia. Therefore, the correct combination is that statements I and II only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_STATEMENT3_Q10 - Mantle cavity ctenidia and radula in molluscs

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding phylum Mollusca:

Statement I: The body of molluscs is unsegmented and divided into a distinct head, muscular foot, and visceral hump.

Statement II: The space between the hump and mantle is the mantle cavity, in which feather-like gills perform only excretory functions.

Statement III: The buccal cavity of molluscs contains a file-like rasping organ called radula used for feeding.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Molluscs are coelomate, soft-bodied invertebrates with a mantle enclosing a pallial cavity, calcareous shell secretion, and a specialized rasping radula.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Proposition
The unsegmented soft molluscan body is structurally organized into three principal regions: an anterior cephalic head, a ventral muscular foot for locomotion, and a dorsal visceral hump holding internal organs. Thus, the first proposition is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Proposition
The feather-like ctenidia situated within the mantle cavity execute dual physiological roles: respiratory gas exchange as well as excretion, not excretion exclusively. Thus, the second proposition is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
The mouth houses the radula, an odontophoral ribbon furnished with transverse rows of chitinous teeth designed for scraping and rasping food substrates. Thus, the third proposition is factually accurate.

Step 5: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
Propositions one and three are scientifically validated, while proposition two incorrectly denies the respiratory role of the ctenidia. Therefore, the correct combination is that statements I and III only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_STATEMENT3_Q11 - Endoskeleton water vascular system and echinoderm excretion

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding phylum Echinodermata:

Statement I: Echinoderms possess a chitinous exoskeleton and an incomplete digestive system with a single opening.

Statement II: The water vascular system in echinoderms plays vital roles in locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration.

Statement III: An excretory system is completely absent in echinoderms, and development is indirect with free-swimming larvae.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Echinoderms are exclusively marine deuterostomes possessing calcareous mesodermal ossicles, ambulacral water canals, complete digestive tracts, and secondary pentaradial symmetry.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Proposition
Echinoderms possess a mesodermally derived endoskeleton composed of calcareous ossicles (not a chitinous exoskeleton) and possess a complete alimentary canal with ventral mouth and dorsal anus. Thus, the first proposition is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Proposition
The hydraulic ambulacral network operates tube feet to coordinate movement, grasp prey items, convey nutrients to the mouth, and facilitate respiratory gas exchange. Thus, the second proposition is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
Echinoderms lack specialized excretory organs, allowing nitrogenous waste to diffuse freely across branchiae and podial walls, and their ontogeny features free-swimming bilateral larvae. Thus, the third proposition is factually accurate.

Step 5: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
Propositions two and three precisely depict the distinctive biology of echinoderms, whereas proposition one misidentifies skeletal origin and digestive morphology. Therefore, the correct combination is that statements II and III only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_STATEMENT3_Q12 - Notochord distribution in protochordates and hemichordate anatomy

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding Hemichordata and Protochordata:

Statement I: Hemichordates have a cylindrical body composed of an anterior proboscis, a collar, and a long trunk, and excrete via a proboscis gland.

Statement II: In subphylum Urochordata, the notochord is present only in the larval tail, whereas in Cephalochordata, it extends from head to tail and persists throughout life.

Statement III: Both Urochordata and Cephalochordata are exclusively marine organisms collectively referred to as protochordates.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Protochordates and hemichordates illuminate key transitional stages in chordate evolution regarding notochord permanence, body regionalization, and excretory specializations.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Proposition
Hemichordates are tripartite marine worms partitioned into preoral proboscis, collar, and elongated trunk, utilizing a vascular proboscis glomerulus gland for excretion. Thus, the first proposition is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Proposition
In Urochordata (tunicates), the notochord is restricted to the tail of the ascidian tadpole and lost during retrogressive metamorphosis, whereas Cephalochordata retain a complete rostro-caudal notochord for life. Thus, the second proposition is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
Urochordates and cephalochordates are strictly marine non-vertebrate chordates grouped taxonomically as protochordates. Thus, the third proposition is factually accurate.

Step 5: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
All three propositions correctly state established morphological and taxonomic realities of hemichordates and protochordates. Therefore, the correct combination is that statements I, II and III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_STATEMENT3_Q13 - Morphological comparisons between cyclostomes and cartilaginous fishes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding Cyclostomata and Chondrichthyes:

Statement I: Cyclostomes have an elongated body with 6-15 pairs of gill slits and a jawless, sucking circular mouth.

Statement II: Chondrichthyes have separate gill slits without an operculum, a cartilaginous endoskeleton, and placoid scales.

Statement III: Chondrichthyes possess an air bladder regulating buoyancy, whereas cyclostomes possess paired pelvic claspers.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Agnathan cyclostomes and gnathostome cartilaginous fishes are differentiated by cranial structure, branchial arches, fins, and integumentary scales.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Proposition
Cyclostomes are jawless ectoparasites bearing an unconstricted suctorial mouth and 6 to 15 pairs of gill apertures for respiration. Thus, the first proposition is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Proposition
Chondrichthyes (sharks and rays) possess exposed gill clefts lacking an opercular flap, a persistent cartilaginous axial skeleton, and backward-pointing placoid dermal denticles. Thus, the second proposition is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
Chondrichthyes lack an air bladder and must swim constantly to avoid sinking; pelvic claspers are present in male Chondrichthyes, not cyclostomes. Thus, the third proposition is incorrect.

Step 5: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
Propositions one and two represent accurate anatomical descriptions, while proposition three falsely attributes air bladders to Chondrichthyes and claspers to cyclostomes. Therefore, the correct combination is that statements I and II only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_ANIMAL_KINGDOM_STATEMENT3_Q14 - Comparative cardiovascular and anatomical features of vertebrates

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding higher vertebrate classes:

Statement I: In Osteichthyes, four pairs of gills are covered by an operculum, and an air bladder regulates buoyancy.

Statement II: Amphibians and all living reptiles possess an incompletely partitioned three-chambered heart without exception.

Statement III: Aves possess pneumatic bones containing air cavities, while mammals are uniquely characterized by the presence of mammary glands.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vertebrates exhibit systematic adaptations across respiratory, circulatory, skeletal, and reproductive systems from bony fishes to tetrapods.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Proposition
Osteichthyes (bony fishes) possess branchial chambers housing four pairs of gill arches shielded by an opercular flap, alongside a hydrostatic swim bladder. Thus, the first proposition is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Proposition
Although amphibians have a three-chambered heart, reptiles include crocodilians which possess a fully four-chambered heart, invalidating the claim of an exceptionless three-chambered condition. Thus, the second proposition is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Proposition
Avian long bones are hollow and pneumatic to reduce flight mass, and mammals possess specialized epidermal hair and glandular mammary tissue to suckle offspring. Thus, the third proposition is factually accurate.

Step 5: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
Propositions one and three correctly outline vertebrate morphology, whereas proposition two overlooks crocodilian heart anatomy. Therefore, the correct combination is that statements I and III only are correct.
